findings.title: Incorrect admin check logic
findings.description: The `require_admin` method uses `if session.role != "admin" or session.role != "owner":` which always evaluates to True, denying access to both admin and owner roles.

findings.title: Session expiration not verified
findings.description: `Authenticator.verify` returns a session without checking `expires_at`, contrary to the docstring that says expired tokens should yield None.

findings.title: Bearer token parsing can raise IndexError
findings.description: `bearer_token` assumes the header contains a space and a token; an empty or malformed header triggers an IndexError.

findings.title: `revoke` may raise KeyError
findings.description: `del self.sessions[token]` assumes the token exists; revoking an unknown token crashes.

findings.title: Cache utilization uses integer division and can divide by zero
findings.description: `utilization` computes `len(self.entries) // self.limit * 100`, producing 0 for any non‑full cache and raising ZeroDivisionError when `limit` is zero.

findings.title: Deleting entries while iterating over the dict
findings.description: `sweep` iterates `for code in self.entries:` and deletes entries inside the loop, which raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`.

findings.title: FETCH_LIMIT environment variable parsed but never applied
findings.description: The code reads `LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT`, parses it, but never stores the value in `cfg.fetch_limit`.

findings.title: `validate` always returns True
findings.description: Even when configuration problems are detected, `validate` prints them but still returns `True`, allowing the service to start with invalid settings.

findings.title: Mutable default argument in `parse_report`
findings.description: The function signature `def parse_report(body, rows=[]):` uses a list that persists across calls, causing rows to accumulate unintentionally.

findings.title: Quota counter key error for new owners
findings.description: `self.quota[owner] = self.quota[owner] + 1` crashes when `owner` is not yet in `self.quota`.

findings.title: Link expiration logic reversed
findings.description: `resolve` deletes a link when `time.time() < link.expires_at` (i.e., when it is still valid) and keeps expired entries, opposite of intended behavior.

findings.title: `success_rate` uses integer division
findings.description: The calculation `used // len(self.links) * 100` truncates the fraction, yielding inaccurate percentages.

findings.title: `top` returns links in ascending hit order
findings.description: Sorting without `reverse=True` gives the least‑followed links first, contrary to the docstring.

findings.title: `by_owner` uses substring match
findings.description: The list comprehension checks `owner in l.owner`, which matches partial names unintentionally.

findings.title: Deleting entries while iterating in `prune`
findings.description: The loop `for code in self.links:` deletes entries during iteration, risking `RuntimeError`.

findings.title: `prune` returns wrong value
findings.description: After pruning, the function returns `len(self.links)` instead of the number of removed entries.

findings.title: `quotas` returns internal mutable dict
findings.description: Returning `self.quota` exposes internal state; callers could mutate it.

findings.title: `warm_cache` does not wait for threads to finish
findings.description: The function spawns threads for each cache set but returns immediately, so callers may assume caching is complete when it is not.

findings.title: `check_targets` may raise IndexError on empty problem list
findings.description: The function returns `problems[0]` without confirming the list is non‑empty, causing an exception when all targets are valid.

findings.title: Iterating over sessions dict without synchronization
findings.description: The `verify` method iterates over `self.sessions.values()` while other threads may add or delete entries via `issue` or `revoke`. Mutating the dictionary during iteration can raise `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`, crashing the service.

findings.title: Session store modified without any locking
findings.description: `issue` and `revoke` write to `self.sessions` without any synchronization. Concurrent calls can corrupt the dictionary or lead to lost or stale sessions, causing authentication failures.

findings.title: Deleting entries while iterating over cache dict
findings.description: `Cache.sweep` iterates `for code in self.entries:` and deletes expired entries inside the loop. Modifying a dictionary during iteration raises a `RuntimeError` and can abort the janitor tick, leaving stale cache entries.

findings.title: Prune removes links while iterating over the dict
findings.description: `Store.prune` iterates `for code in self.links:` and deletes entries inside the loop. This mutates the dictionary during iteration, causing a `RuntimeError` and potentially leaving the store in an inconsistent state.

findings.title: Unsynchronized deletion of links in resolve()
findings.description: `Store.resolve` deletes an entry (`del self.links[code]`) without any synchronization. If the janitor thread or another request modifies `self.links` concurrently, this can cause a `RuntimeError` or lost updates, breaking link lookup semantics.

findings.title: Janitor thread mutates store.links without lock
findings.description: The janitor loop directly executes `del store.links[code]` on the shared `Store.links` dict. This bypasses any synchronization the `Store` class might add, resulting in race conditions with request handlers that also read or write `store.links`.

findings.title: Concurrent CSV export writes can clobber each other
findings.description: `export_csv` opens the target file for writing without any exclusivity. If multiple requests export with the same `name` concurrently, they will overwrite each other's output, leading to corrupted reports.

findings.title: Predictable session tokens
findings.description: Session tokens are generated with `random.getrandbits`, which is not cryptographically secure. An attacker who can infer the PRNG state can predict future tokens and hijack sessions.

findings.title: Missing session expiration check
findings.description: `Authenticator.verify` returns a session without checking `expires_at`, so tokens remain valid indefinitely after the configured 12‑hour TTL, allowing long‑term unauthorized access.

findings.title: Hardcoded default secret
findings.description: When `LINKD_SECRET` is unset, the code falls back to the literal `dev-secret-do-not-use`, a predictable value that could be used to sign or verify tokens if the secret ever becomes part of a HMAC operation.

findings.title: Unsalted SHA‑256 password hashing
findings.description: Passwords are hashed with plain SHA‑256 without a salt, making them vulnerable to rainbow‑table attacks and fast offline cracking.

findings.title: Admin quotas endpoint lacks authentication
findings.description: The `/admin/quotas` handler authorizes solely on an `x-admin: true` header, without verifying the requester's session or role, allowing any client to retrieve quota data.

findings.title: Open redirect in `/out` endpoint
findings.description: The `out` handler redirects to a user‑supplied `next` URL without validation, enabling phishing or malicious redirects.

findings.title: Directory traversal in CSV export
findings.description: `export_csv` builds a file path with `os.path.join(directory, name + ".csv")` where `name` is user‑controlled. Supplying `../` sequences lets an attacker write files outside the export directory, potentially overwriting system files.

findings.title: Arbitrary file read via export report
findings.description: `read_report` reads a file assembled from the user‑controlled `name` without validation, allowing an attacker to read any file the process can access via path traversal.

findings.title: Symlink race on snapshot write
findings.description: `write_snapshot` writes to a fixed temporary path `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json` then renames it. An attacker who can create a symlink at that path can cause the rename to overwrite arbitrary files.

findings.title: Dictionary mutation during sweep
findings.description: `sweep` iterates over `self.entries` while deleting keys, which raises `RuntimeError` and can crash the janitor thread, disabling cache eviction.

findings.title: Expiration logic reversed in link resolution
findings.description: `Store.resolve` deletes a link when the current time is **before** its expiry and returns the target after expiry, causing valid links to disappear and expired links to remain usable.

findings.title: CORS wildcard with credentials
findings.description: The response sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: "*"` together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: "true"`, a misconfiguration that can enable CSRF attacks if a browser or proxy ignores the violation.
